ideas.title: My hair grows toward you
ideas.critique: This is round 1's 'I grow out while you're away' again, now aimed at the lens. Lumi changes its body, catches friends, carries them and throws them off with a click, which is the jelly-ball recipe with hair instead of glass. Verlet strands that steer toward the viewer and blur the frame edges are new motion and material, but only if they sway and curl with weight. Stiff tubes that pop back in a frame would make it one more Lumi transformation.

ideas.title: My shadow quits
ideas.critique: A character made only of light, cast by a body no camera sees, is something only a path tracer can do. It bends over the trunk, the grass and the water for free and stretches to its real length at sunset, so it is strong. It depends on the shadow being readable as Lumi and moving like a character with intent. A vague grey blob sliding at noon would waste the trick, and friends jumping onto it is the most guessable beat.

ideas.title: The island sings your wish as a round
ideas.critique: This is 'Hum of the island' again with the human's typed wish as the score, and friends coming in one after another echoes the word passed down a row. Real sound for the first time, with a voice that fits each body and beaks moving on time, is a real step. It falls flat if the formant voices sound like buzzing beeps or the canon turns to mush, and the whole value depends on that.

ideas.title: Wrong bodies at noon
ideas.critique: Keeping the gaits and swapping the meshes could give odd new motion, like a crab's scuttle driving a pig or a cloud rolling. Made plainly, though, it is a timed island-wide event where everyone acts strange for a while and then it resets, which is the recent world-rule formula. Mixing body parts was already done in the breeding pen. The gag only works if each wrong body really fails in its own physical way, not just slides along on the wrong skeleton.

ideas.title: Lumi breathes on the screen
ideas.critique: A real dielectric pane with a fog roughness map that Lumi paints is a strong materials showcase, and the island has never had a surface between it and the viewer. Lumi coming to the lens and the doodle of the imagined human are the sentimental fourth-wall beat the pitch makes you expect. After the fog it is one close shot of Lumi drawing, so there is little to watch twice.
